dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2301.text: A bird plump and large, 𨾊𨾊. From 隹; 工 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2302.text: The action 繳𩀼, apparently shooting with a corded arrow. From 隹; 㪔 supplies the sound. Another explanation: the flight described as 飛𩀼. [The descriptive words are uncertain.]

shuowen:2303.text: To shoot flying birds with a corded arrow. From 隹; 弋 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2304.text: The male parent among birds. From 隹; 厷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2305.text: The female parent among birds. From 隹; 此 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2306.text: To cover birds so they cannot fly or run away. From 网 and 隹. Pronounced like 到.

shuowen:2307.text: Fat meat. From 弓, that with which one shoots 隹. Changsha has Xiajuan county.

shuowen:2308.text: To fly. From 隹; 隓 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2309.text: A bird spreading its feathers and rousing itself. From 大 and 隹. All graphs in this category contain 奞. Pronounced like 睢.

shuowen:2310.text: To hold a bird in the hand and lose it. From 又 and 奞.

shuowen:2311.text: To fly broadly. From 奞 above 田. The Odes says: “Unable to rise in flight.”

shuowen:2312.text: A kind of owl. From 隹 and 𦫳, with feathered horns. Where it calls, the people suffer calamity. All graphs in this category contain 雈. Pronounced like 和.

shuowen:2313.text: To measure and assess. From 又 holding 雈. Another explanation: a hurried look; another: 蒦 means to measure.

shuowen:2314.text: A small sparrow. From 雈; 吅 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “The 雚 calls on the mound.”

shuowen:2315.text: 𨾦舊, the bird 舊畱. From 雈; 臼 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2316.text: Sheep's horns. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 𦫳. Pronounced like 𦮃.

shuowen:2317.text: To oppose or turn away. From 𦫳 and 兆; 兆 is the ancient form of 別.

shuowen:2318.text: To match one another. The explanation is missing. Pronounced like 宀.

shuowen:2319.text: Eyes not properly aligned. From 𦫳 and 目. All graphs in this category contain 𥄕. 萈 contains it. Pronounced like 末.

shuowen:2320.text: Eyes not seeing clearly. From 𥄕 and 䀏; 䀏 means repeated movement of the eyes.

shuowen:2321.text: Fire not bright. From 𥄕 and 火; 𥄕 also supplies the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Spread layered 𤊾 mats,” meaning woven rush mats. Pronounced the same as 蔑.

shuowen:2322.text: Tired eyes without brightness. From 𥄕: a tired person looks weary; also from 戍.

shuowen:2323.text: Auspicious. From 𦫳, depicting head, horns, feet and tail. Confucius said: “The characters for cattle and sheep represent them through their forms.” All graphs in this category contain 羊.

shuowen:2324.text: The bleating of sheep. From 羊, depicting vocal breath rising. It shares the idea of 牟.

shuowen:2325.text: A lamb. From 羊; abbreviated 照 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2326.text: A five-month-old lamb. From 羊; 宁 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 煑.

shuowen:2327.text: A six-month-old lamb. From 羊; 敄 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 霧.

shuowen:2328.text: A small sheep. From 羊; 大 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 達.

shuowen:2329.text: A sheep not yet a full year old. From 羊; 兆 supplies the sound. Some say a 夷 sheep weighing around a hundred jin is 䍮. Pronounced like 洮 in the Spring and Autumn's “Covenant at Tao.”

shuowen:2330.text: A ram. From 羊; 氐 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2331.text: A 牂 sheep. From 羊; 分 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2332.text: A ram. From 羊; 爿 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2333.text: A male 夏 sheep is called 羭. From 羊; 俞 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2334.text: A male 夏 sheep is called 羖. From 羊; 殳 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2335.text: A castrated 羖 sheep. From 羊; 曷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2336.text: A castrated sheep. From 羊; 夷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2337.text: A sheep with a yellow belly. From 羊; 番 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2338.text: The name of a sheep. From 羊; 巠 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2339.text: The name of a sheep. From 羊; 執 supplies the sound. Pingyu in Runan has a 𦎷 station. Pronounced like 晉.

shuowen:2340.text: Thin. From 羊; 𣎆 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2341.text: Sheep pressing against one another. From 羊; 委 supplies the sound. [The action 𦎸 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2342.text: The action 䍴𦎸, sheep pressing together. From 羊; 責 supplies the sound. [The exact action is uncertain.]

shuowen:2343.text: A group. From 羊; 君 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2344.text: A flock of sheep pressing against one another. Another explanation: a black sheep. From 羊; 垔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2345.text: The name of a sheep whose hoof skin can cut lacquer. From 羊; 此 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2346.text: Sweet or delicious. From 羊 and 大. Among the six domestic animals, sheep chiefly supply food. 美 and 善 share the same idea.

shuowen:2347.text: Shepherds among the western Rong. From 人 and 羊; 羊 also supplies the sound. The southern 蠻 and 閩 contain 虫; northern 狄 contains 犬; eastern 貉 contains 豸; western 羌 contains 羊: these are six kinds. Southwestern 僰 and 僬僥 contain 人: perhaps, occupying the kun quarter, they have a somewhat compliant nature. Only eastern 夷 contains 大; 大 means a person. Yi customs are benevolent; the benevolent live long, and there is a country of gentlemen who do not die. Confucius said: “The Way is not practiced; I wish to go to the Nine Yi, taking a raft to float on the sea.” There was a reason for this.

shuowen:2348.text: To advance goodness. From 羊; 久 supplies the sound. King Wen was imprisoned at Youli, in Tangyin.

shuowen:2349.text: The smell of sheep. From three 羊. All graphs in this category contain 羴.

shuowen:2350.text: Sheep mingling together. From 羴 beneath 尸; 尸 means a house. Another explanation: coming forward ahead of one another.

shuowen:2351.text: The gaze of hawks and falcons. From 隹 and 䀠; 䀠 also supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 瞿. Pronounced like 句 in 章句.

shuowen:2352.text: A bird about to dart away. From 又 holding it, the restless manner 矍矍. Pronounced like 穬 in the Odes' “Mighty are those Huai Yi.” Another explanation: a hurried look.

shuowen:2353.text: A pair of birds. From two 隹. All graphs in this category contain 雔. Pronounced like 醻.

shuowen:2354.text: The sound of flight: a pair flying in rain makes a 靃 sound.

shuowen:2355.text: Two birds. From 雔 held by 又.

shuowen:2356.text: A flock of birds. From three 隹. All graphs in this category contain 雥.

shuowen:2357.text: A flock of birds. From 雥; 𣶒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2358.text: A flock of birds in a tree. From 雥 and 木.

shuowen:2359.text: A general name for long-tailed birds. A pictograph. A bird's foot resembles 匕, hence from 匕. All graphs in this category contain 鳥.

shuowen:2360.text: A divine bird. Tianlao said: “Its front is a wild goose's, rear a unicorn's, neck a snake's, tail a fish's; forehead a stork's, cheeks a mandarin duck's; dragon pattern, tiger back, swallow jaw, chicken beak, all five colors complete. It emerges from the eastern country of gentlemen, soars beyond the four seas, passes Kunlun, drinks at Dizhu, washes its feathers in Weak Water, and roosts at dusk in Wind Cave. When it appears, all under heaven enjoys great peace.” From 鳥; 凡 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2361.text: Also an essence of divine numinous power. Red, with five colors, chicken-shaped; its call accords with the five notes, and it arrives when songs of praise arise. From 鳥; 䜌 supplies the sound. In King Cheng of Zhou's time the Di and Qiang presented a luan bird.

shuowen:2362.text: 鸑鷟, a phoenix kind, a divine bird. From 鳥; 獄 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: “At Zhou's rise, the 鸑鷟 called on Mount Qi.” In the Yangtze there is also a 鸑鷟, resembling a duck but larger, with red eyes.

shuowen:2363.text: The bird 鸑鷟. From 鳥; 族 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2364.text: 鷫鷞, among the divine birds of the five directions: east 發明, south 焦明, west 鷫鷞, north 幽昌, center 鳳皇. From 鳥; 肅 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2365.text: The bird 鷫鷞. From 鳥; 爽 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2366.text: The bird 鹘鵃. From 鳥; 九 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2367.text: The bird 鶌鳩. From 鳥; 屈 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2368.text: The bird 祝鳩. From 鳥; 隹 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2369.text: The bird 鶻鵃. From 鳥; 骨 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2370.text: The bird 鶻鵃. From 鳥; 舟 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2371.text: 秸𪈅, the bird 尸鳩. From 鳥; 𥱩 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2372.text: A kind of dove. From 鳥; 合 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2373.text: The bird 渴鴠. From 鳥; 旦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2374.text: The shrike, 伯勞. From 鳥; 狊 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2375.text: The bird 天龠. From 鳥; 翏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2376.text: The bird 卑居. From 鳥; 與 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2377.text: 雗鷽, a mountain magpie, a bird knowing future events. From 鳥; abbreviated 學 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2378.text: A black bird with many young. Music Master Kuang says: “In the south is a bird called 羌𪆩, with a yellow head and red eyes, all five colors complete.” From 鳥; 就 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2379.text: 鴟鴞, namely 寕鴂. From 鳥; 号 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2380.text: The bird 寕鴂. From 鳥; 夬 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2381.text: A bird. From 鳥; 祟 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2382.text: The bird 澤虞. From 鳥; 方 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2383.text: A bird. From 鳥; 𢧵 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2384.text: A bird. From 鳥; 桼 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2385.text: The bird 鋪豉. From 鳥; 失 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2386.text: The bird 鶤雞. From 鳥; 軍 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 運.

shuowen:2387.text: A bird. From 鳥; 芺 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2388.text: A bird. From 鳥; 臼 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2389.text: 𪆄𪃐, the bird 桃蟲. From 鳥; 焦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2390.text: The bird 𪆄𪃐. From 鳥; 眇 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2391.text: A bird beautiful when young and ugly when grown is called 𪅳離. From 鳥; 畱 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2392.text: A bird. From 鳥; 堇 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2393.text: The bird 欺老. From 鳥; 彖 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2394.text: A bird. From 鳥; abbreviated 說 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2395.text: A bird. From 鳥; 主 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2396.text: A bird. From 鳥; 昏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2397.text: 刀鷯, which splits reeds and eats the insects inside. From 鳥; 𤋯 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2398.text: A bird whose female is 皇. From 鳥; 匽 supplies the sound. Another explanation: the phoenix.

shuowen:2399.text: The bird 瞑鴲. From 鳥; 旨 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2400.text: The bird 烏鸔. From 鳥; 各 supplies the sound.
